item.title: Cowboys Skip Deadline Splashes To Bet On Existing Talent
item.description: Robert Goddin-Imagn Images The Dallas Cowboys stayed quiet at the trade deadline. While other teams scrambled for last-minute upgrades, Dallas decided to trust the players already in the building. ESPN insider Adam Schefter noted that the organization never appeared close to making another major deal. “It never sounded like they got close to making any big deals,” Schefter said, adding that there was no real movement on a George Pickens trade. This approach puts the pressure squarely on the current squad to deliver results over the final eight games. Why The Roster Stays Put General Manager Jerry Jones and the front office clearly believe they have enough pieces to win. They already spent a 2028 second-round pick earlier in the season to add cornerback Joey Porter Jr. from the Pittsburgh Steelers. That move gave the secondary a physical presence without burning up all their draft capital. The team said the addition was an aggressive upgrade to the roster. “Rather than surrender more draft capital, the organization will give its existing players an opportunity to deliver,” the report states. In the last game on Sunday, Nov. 8, Prescott threw for 335 yards and two touchdowns against Indianapolis. CeeDee Lamb caught 10 passes for 195 yards, proving he can dominate when given the ball. Javonte Williams also ran for 101 yards and a score, showing the run game can keep defenses honest. However, the defense faces a much harder test in the next matchup. In his last four games, Quinnen Williams has recorded 10 tackles for loss and four sacks, marking a recent standout performance. The Challenge Looming Sunday San Francisco enters the stadium on Sunday, Nov. 15, with a 7-1 record and a six-game winning streak. They are not just a good team; they have beaten Dallas in their last four meetings, including two playoff games. The 49ers added Keenan Allen to their squad before the deadline for a 2027 sixth-round pick. His arrival adds another layer of difficulty for a Cowboys defense that needs to limit explosive plays. Dallas coach Brian Schottenheimer admitted that tight end Jake Ferguson and running back Tyler Goodson will miss multiple weeks due to knee injuries. “A lot of these guys, they play on adrenaline,” Schottenheimer said, highlighting the team’s resilience despite these setbacks, according to WJOX-FM . They need consistent performances to keep their playoff hopes alive. “The Cowboys still believe they have the talent they need to make a late second half of the season push here,” Schefter added. The next game starts at 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday, Nov. 15, at AT&T Stadium when the San Francisco 49ers visit the Dallas Cowboys.

item.title: England's Mitchell could miss Six Nations after hamstring operation
item.description: Mitchell's four hamstring injuries this year have not all been on the same leg, with three to his right and one to his left [Getty Images] England scrum-half Alex Mitchell could miss next year's Six Nations after an operation to fix recurring hamstring issues. The 29-year-old, who was Steve Borthwick's first-choice nine last season, has gone under the knife after suffering four hamstring injuries this year. If Mitchell, who has recovered ahead of schedule in the past, follows an estimated four-month rehabilitation it would give him a chance of playing in England's final two matches, against Wales and Scotland on 6 and 13 March. Any setback however would leave him with only pre-tournament friendlies to play in for England before next year's Rugby World Cup in Australia. Mitchell's latest hamstring injury, which came in Northampton's win over Gloucester last month, ruled him out of this month's Nations Championship campaign. Mitchell suffered an injury to the same hamstring against Ireland in February and again against Fiji in July. He also tweaked his other hamstring - his left, non-kicking leg - in an England training camp in May. Mitchell told the i Paper last month that he had been given the option, like skipper Maro Itoje, to skip England's summer fixtures against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina, but opted to play instead. While Jack van Poortvliet has emerged as Borthwick's starting pick in Mitchell's absence, there is competition behind the Leicester man with Bristol's Harry Randall, Bath's Ben Spencer and Mitchell's club team-mate Archie McParland all vying for position. Mitchell travelled to Finland to be operated on by Lasse Lempainen, a specialist in elite sporting injuries. Chelsea and England defender Reece James and Paris St-Germain's Ballon D'Or winner Ousmane Dembele are among Lempainen's previous patients, both returning to consistent playing time after a string of muscular injuries. Mitchell's England team-mate Ben Curry was also operated on by Lempainen and has made a successful return to action after 10 months out, featuring in England's win over Australia last weekend. item.title: Ghana kick-start Afcon 2027 bid despite Ayew penalty miss
item.description: Jordan Ayew joined Championship side Sheffield United in September after spending two seasons with Leicester City [Getty Images] Ghana belatedly kick-started their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) qualifying campaign with a 2-0 home win over Somalia. The Black Stars had lost their opening two Group C matches against Ivory Coast and The Gambia, leading to the departure of coach Carlos Queiroz by mutual consent. Ghana women's coach Kim Bjorkegren was placed in interim charge for this month's double-header against the Ocean Stars, with the West Africans in danger of missing a second successive edition of the Afcon finals. The hosts were given a chance to take an early lead in Sekondi-Takoradi after Alidu Seidu was pulled down in the box, but Jordan Ayew's 14th-minute penalty was saved by Somalia goalkeeper Ibrahim Hussein. Ghana did go ahead in first-half stoppage time when Mohammed Salisu headed Mohammed Kudus's deep corner back across goal and Jonas Adjetey nodded in from six yards out. Felix Afena-Gyan doubled the Black Stars' advantage just after the hour mark when his shot from inside the box squirmed under Hussein and over the line. The result puts the four-time continental champions three points behind Ivory Coast and The Gambia, who meet in Bouake at 19:00 GMT. Cameroon, DR Congo and Senegal are also in action among seven other Afcon 2027 qualifiers on Thursday.

item.title: Alysa Liu speaks on new winning mentality in Life magazine cover story
item.description: This winter, Alysa Liu was the name on everyone's lips. The skating star, who hails from Oakland, wowed audiences around the world when she won the individual gold medal at the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan . She also won the group gold with Team USA. The then-20-year-old captured attention with her confidence in her individuality, including a striped hairstyle and a "smiley" piercing. She is now taking a break and is not competing in the 2026-27 season , but promises "I have a plan" in her cover story for LIFE Magazine that was published online Thursday, Nov. 12. The publication will return to print on Nov. 23, which is 90 years after its first issue. The comeback arrives after a nearly 20-year hiatus. Liu is the first of five cover stars that will be featured on the first edition of the re-upped quarterly magazine. The story, written by Bonnie Tsui, is accompanied by striking photographs by Spike Jonze of Liu skating in a flowing red outfit in a darkened rink. The feature reflects on Liu's previous time stepping away from the sport during the COVID pandemic. She realized that she wasn't skating for herself, but to please others. "When I was younger, I wanted to win all the time," she said. "But winning was really about getting reassurance from my coach and my dad, and just making them happy, making them think I was, like, perfect or something." In the piece, Liu shows the many sides of her life after fame. She trains at the Yerba Buena Ice Skating & Bowling Center in San Francisco, carefully crafting her next routines with her coaches Phillip DiGuglielmo and Massimo Scali. She has a lunch full of laughs at A16, a pizzeria in Oakland, with her closest friends. Liu explained how her perspective in being open with the world has changed since rising to superstardom. She's not only become a sports icon, but has become a well-known name is fashion, attending the Met Gala and Paris Fashion Week. "I don’t really like hiding stuff about myself," she said. "But now, I low-key have to, to protect my peace." She pondered how taking ownership of her sport allowed her to travel with her siblings and makes her excited to support her United States teammates from the stands, emphasizing how she values camaraderie. Liu said at the peak of her unhappiness she "would cry all the time – like, every session – and not in a good way." But she has no regrets. "If I went back in time, I would still want myself to go through everything, just so I could come to my own conclusion," she said. "Now, I don’t look to other people to find my happiness anymore. That has changed the definition of winning for me." Fans can pre-order their copy of LIFE Magazine featuring Liu online or purchase a magazine at select retailers on Nov. 23. item.title: CJ McCollum joins NBA on Prime crew, discusses role on Hawks, Damian Lillard's comeback
item.description: CJ McCollum hit the game-winning shot in the Atlanta Hawks ' Game 3 victory over the New York Knicks in the first round of last year's playoffs. Not only does he remember that shot, but he remembers enjoying being a guest on Prime Video's "NBA Nightcap" postgame show where he appeared in his pajamas and the hosts joked he put the Knicks "to sleep." They all laughed about his role of villain as his son popped in to say hello. The party doesn't have to stop there as NBA on Prime announced on Thursday, Nov. 12 that the 14-year veteran guard will be a player commentator for several programs this season starting with "NBA Nightcap" on Friday, Nov. 13. "The conversation and team analysis that night was really fun," he told USA TODAY Sports of the postgame memories, "and I thought the chemistry was there, and I felt like it made a lot of sense (for me to join the Prime team). And I have a great appreciation for what NBA on Prime is doing, what the crew is doing, and how they educate and share authentic analysis." McCollum, 35, majored in journalism at Lehigh University and has experience hosting his own podcast with "The CJ McCollum Show" and "Pull Up with CJ McCollum." Among Prime's All-Star team of talent that he is joining is a mix of longtime broadcasters, including Kevin Harlan, and basketball greats like Udonis Haslem, Dirk Nowitzki, Steve Nash and Candace Parker. McCollum said the team is "a really cool atmosphere, really great environment of people that I respect and admire." "They're very honest. They watch the game. They're students of the game. They’re people who appreciate the game and they do a great job of describing why certain things are happening," he continued. "... When you have that group of professionals who have played the game, have talked the game, have lived the game, have been around it and seen it for so long, you get various impactful moments where viewers are able to really get a glimpse of what's actually happening, why it's happening, in an insightful way that they can digest." McCollum appreciates the craft of journalism and how showing the human element of any story brings people together. As journalism continues to face industry challenges , the 2016 Most Improved Player has hope. "Storytelling is vital. I think it makes the world a better place," he said. "Being able to hear people's stories, being able to see people's journeys not just in the sports world but in life, I think is something that we all can appreciate. "And journalism isn't dying. It's just evolving. But I think the people who move with integrity, who do things the right way and really appreciate the craft are continuing to thrive for sure." item.title: CJ McCollum Is Still in the NBA — Why Is He Taking a TV Analyst Job?
item.description: CJ McCollum - CJ McCollum (Paras Griffin/Getty Images) CJ McCollum might still be hitting key shots for the Atlanta Hawks on the court, but the 13-year NBA veteran is adding another major media gig to his resume. Prime Video announced that McCollum is joining the NBA on Prime broadcast team as a player contributor for the 2026–27 season. The former National Basketball Players Association (NBPA) president will make select studio appearances throughout the year, kicking off his run on NBA Nightcap following Friday’s Emirates NBA Cup slate, which features a game between the New York Knicks and Indiana Pacers. The 35-year-old athlete isn’t a stranger to balancing both worlds. With a journalism degree from Lehigh University and a history of digital media ventures—including hosting and executive producing his ReMaking America talk show on PlayersTV—he has long prepared for life outside the court. “So much has changed about how fans experience the game, and I’m excited to join Prime Video to share something only a player can: what’s really going on in the locker room, on the floor, and in the league right now,” McCollum said in a statement. “I’m still a player first, but this was too good an opportunity to pass up.” Prime Video leadership is equally enthusiastic about what his perspective as an active player can bring to their second season of coverage. “We’re thrilled to have CJ join NBA on Prime,” Amina Hussein, Prime Video Head of On-Air Talent and Development, also said in the statement. “As a 13-year veteran and former NBPA president, he brings a unique insight that our viewers want to hear. His ability to connect with fans and give his perspective on a specific play, or the reason behind a certain outcome, makes him a perfect fit for our second season of NBA on Prime.” Related Fans Compare ABC’s New Shaquille O’Neal Hide-and-Seek Show to a '30 Rock' Joke McCollum certainly has the resume to back it up. He was named the NBA’s Most Improved Player in 2016, when he broke out as a dynamic scorer with the Portland Trail Blazers and helped lead the franchise to the 2019 Western Conference Finals. Over a career spanning more than a decade, he has amassed over 16,000 points and averaged 20 or more points per game for over 10 consecutive seasons. Having also served as president of the NBPA from 2021 to 2025, McCollum brings a rare administrative and on-court vantage point to the desk. Even as he navigates transitioning to a bench role with the Hawks this season, McCollum follows in the footsteps of other active NBA players like Golden States Warriors forward Draymond Green—who serves as a guest analyst on Inside the NBA and hosts The Draymond Green Show —as well as fellow NBA on Prime contributors Kyle Lowry and Tyrese Haliburton , who have stepped onto the analyst desk while still playing on the court. item.title: Mark Daigneault provides injury update on Thomas Sorber
item.description: Habitually going through pregame warmups all of the 2026-27 regular season, Thomas Sorber awaits his NBA debut. The 20-year-old continues to recover from a follow-up knee procedure he had in July. Once viewed as a four-week timetable, it's been four months without being given the green light to go. The Oklahoma City Thunder badly need NBA-capable bodies. As evident in their two losses to the Portland Trail Blazers on their recent back-to-back. item.description: 1979 Toyota Celica 2000GT RA45 Group 4. Image credit: TTTNIS/Wikimedia Commons (CC0) Everyone will write about the badge. Fair enough: the Celica name, which carried Carlos Sainz to world titles in 1990 and 1992, is back on a Rally1 car for 2027. But the nameplate is the least interesting part of Toyota’s announcement. The detail worth your attention is the structure behind it: two teams, two cars, and, by Toyota’s own account, the same power and performance in both. My read: this is less a heritage stunt than a hedge, and a bolder one than it looks. Toyota has put its strongest 2026 drivers behind the new name and left the old one to the comeback cast. That choice tells you where the company expects its pressure, and its proof, to come from. What Toyota actually confirmed On 3 November, TOYOTA GAZOO Racing laid out a 2027 line-up split across two entries that both run out of the team’s Jyväskylä base. TOYOTA RACING will run the GR Celica Rally1 for Elfyn Evans and Scott Martin, Oliver Solberg and Elliott Edmondson, and Sami Pajari and Marko Salminen. GAZOO Racing TOYOTA will run the GR Yaris Rally1 for Ott Tänak and Martin Järveoja, Takamoto Katsuta and Aaron Johnston, and Kalle Rovanperä and Jonne Halttunen on a partial season of selected events. Both cars are built to the new WRC Car regulations. Toyota says they will have equal power and performance, that homologation is due before the end of 2026, and that further details and liveries will follow before the season. Up to six factory cars can start a given rally. Sébastien Ogier may make selected appearances. What the release does not give you is an engine specification, any description of how the two cars differ, or a single word about a road-going Celica. Anything on that last point is speculation. Elfyn Evans, pictured in a GR Yaris Rally1 at the 2023 Central European Rally, moves to the Celica-badged team for 2027. Evans won the 2026 drivers’ title by five points over Solberg and six over Pajari. Those are the top three in the final standings, and all three are in the Celica. Toyota did not hide its new nameplate behind a development driver or a part-timer. It handed it to the champion and the two men who came closest to beating him. item.title: I managed Wrexham - Phil Parkinson needs to follow my lead to get best out of his team
item.description: Wrexham will face Lincoln City after the international break -Credit:GETTY Every manager will have a philosophy, a preferred way of playing and, ideally, a preferred starting eleven. But football has a habit of ripping up even the best-laid plans. Injuries, illness, loss of form, suspensions, attitude and a whole host of other factors can quickly turn a managers carefully constructed blueprint on its head. That is when flexibility, both tactically and within the squad, becomes so important. The past week has been a good example of how a relatively small tactical adjustment can make a significant difference, particularly when a squad is being ravaged by injuries in key attacking areas. With three creative players unavailable, alongside the new long-term injury to Sam Smith (wishing him a speedy recovery), Phil Parkinson has been forced to revisit a familiar formation from our League One campaign. Without our recognised ‘number 10s’, he has returned to a midfield three, with one holding midfielder, or ‘6’, and two more advanced ‘8s’, rather than the previous system of two deeper midfielders and two attacking tens. For me, it brought greater balance. Against Blackburn, Todd Cantwell had found plenty of joy drifting into the wide areas when we were playing with narrow deep midfielders, a number 10 and two strikers. The change helped provide greater defensive stability, but it also offered something going forward. The two ‘8s’ were given more licence to get beyond the ball, link up with the wing-backs and connect with the strikers. It gave us different options and, importantly, a better balance between attack and defence. • All the Phil Parkinson questions you wanted to know but were afraid to ask • Phil Parkinson may need to change his trusted approach to get Wrexham fans back on side Would that change have happened if everyone had been fit? Probably not. And that’s where management becomes interesting. There was another calculated gamble in moving Lewis O’Brien into the number 10 role, playing just off Kieffer Moore. It isn’t a natural position for Lewis, who generally prefers to operate from deeper areas, but he certainly possesses some of the attributes required. His energy allows him to lead the press, he anticipates situations well and his movement can cause opponents problems. It’s a risk when a player hasn’t regularly occupied that position, but Parkinson’s options are limited and sometimes necessity forces your hand. This is where a manager needs a little bit of creative thinking, and perhaps a slice of luck. A new combination clicks, a player discovers a position that suits him or somebody takes an unexpected opportunity and makes it their own. Of course, it doesn’t always work! Brian Flynn and Peter Reid both decided that playing me at right midfield might be the answer at various points in my career. Let’s just say those particular experiments weren’t quite as successful! Lewis O'Brien put in a brilliant performance in the No.10 role -Cred

item.title: Five games you won't want to miss this international break
item.description: Five games you won't want to miss this international break The international break is here and there are some massive match-ups to keep the intrigue ahead of club football's return. From Nations League showdowns between European giants, to a South American blockbuster between fierce rivals, here are the matches you don't want to miss. Italy vs France Thursday 12th November, kick-off 7:45pm GMT France face Italy on Thursday night, as Group A's top two collide. A win for the visitors will seal top spot, though Italy can climb above France with a win of their own. Roberto Mancini's second spell as Italy manager began with a disappointing defeat to Belgium, before an emphatic 4-1 win in Türkye kept them in contention to win the group. Italy are in a rebuild and this will be a good assessment of their progress, against a Kylian Mbappe-less French. Netherlands vs Greece Friday 13th November, kick-off 7:45pm GMT There's another table-topping Nations League clash on Friday night, as the Netherlands take on Greece in Amsterdam. The teams are locked together on eight points at the top of the group, with both unbeaten after four games. Greece are aiming to continue their impressive recent record on the road, after wins in Germany and Serbia earlier in the group. Argentina vs Uruguay Friday 13th November, kick-off 11pm GMT A Clasico del Rio de la Plata at La Bombenera, don't mind if we do. Argentine are out to prove there's life after Lionel Messi during a high-profile friendly against fierce rivals Uruguay. La Albiceleste head into unchartered waters without their talismanic icon, following Messi's decision to retire from international football. Uruguay are also in the midst of uncertainty, with former favourite Diego Forlan in interim charge, after Marcelo Bielsa's exit. Spain vs England Sunday 15th November, kick-off 7:45pm GMT Both sides have challenges to navigate first, but Spain and England could be set for a group-deciding contest on Sunday evening. The world champions have a perfect record after four games, which includes a 3-2 win at Wembley. England have kept pace with them since that defeat, and thrashed Croatia 7-0 in a statement of intent during the previous break. Spain are world football's best international side right now, and England must show they can compete. Germany vs Netherlands Monday 16th November, kick-off 7:45pm GMT One of the biggest rivalries in international football returns as Germany meet the Netherlands on Monday night. Jurgen Klopp's start as Germany head coach has been underwhelming, with Die Mannschaft winning one of their first four games in the group. The Netherlands, in contrast, are unbeaten after four games, though did require a 92nd-minute Cody Gakpo equaliser to rescue a result in the return fixture.

item.title: U19 Euros Qualifiers: Winning start for Germany after late comeback against Sweden
item.description: U19 Euros Qualifiers: Winning start for Germany after late comeback against Sweden Germany started the second round of the U19 European Championship qualifying campaign with three points after their comeback victory over their Swedish counterparts. All the three goals of the game in Portugal were scored in the last 20 minutes. The match was initially planned for Wednesday before it had to be postponed for the next day due to extreme weather. With the assistant coach Pascal Pellowski taking charge in place of the suspended Hanno Balistch, Germany U19 only had a single shot on target in the first 45 minutes. Substitute Ahmed Saeed put Sweden in front from close range fifteen minutes before time. However, Germany found their way back in the game as two substitutes scored in the final five minutes of regular time. Debutant Kevin Ekweribe tied the score after a cross from fellow Köln attacker Maik Akumu. Germany went on to push for the winner as Swedish goalkeeper John-Oliver Lacayo denied Noah Ringbeck a winning goal with a brilliant save. Sweden failed to clear the resulting corner-kick from Mathieu Nguefack as Niklas Scheller completed the comeback from close range to secure a narrow victory for Germany in the opening game of Group A3. Last year's finalists will face hosts Portugal and Lithuania in the next five days as they now have a huge chance to advance for the Elite Round. Portugal beat Lithuania in the other game from the group as they also relied on a late goal. Germany's victory was shadowed by another injury setback for Cassiano Kiala as the FC Bayern talent had to be subbed off early in the second-half. The center-back has only returned from a long-term injury in August.

item.title: New Carlos Alcaraz fitness update emerges ahead of ATP Finals amid concern over knee bandage
item.description: Carlos Alcaraz will continue his quest for a maiden ATP Finals title next week in Turin. The 23-year-old Spaniard, who completed the Career Grand Slam by winning the Australian Open earlier this season, has never won the ATP Finals. Alcaraz has made three appearances at the year-end tournament in his career and achieved his best result last year by reaching the final, where he ultimately fell to rival Jannik Sinner. Concerns were sparked on social media after Alcaraz was seen wearing tape on his knee while training in Turin ahead of the ATP Finals. Photo by HELMUT FOHRINGER / APA / AFP via Getty Images Update on Carlos Alcaraz’s knee tape issued amid concerns According to Spanish journalist Alvaro Sanchez, the bandage is nothing to be too concerned about. In a post on X , formerly known as Twitter, Sanchez said: “Some of you are asking me about Carlos Alcaraz’s knee, which he trained with a bandage on yesterday in Turin. “What I’m being told is that it’s a precautionary measure for a niggle he’s been carrying since the semifinals in Paris. As of today, there’s no real danger. That said, with injuries and niggles, you never know, and I think it’s the right call for the team to take these precautions to minimize risks in case anything happens. Stay calm.” Alcaraz has enjoyed a successful but lengthy indoor hard court season thus far, which started with a triumph at the Vienna Open. Alcaraz won the ATP 500 tournament in Vienna without dropping a set, and carried that momentum into the Paris Masters. Following three consecutive years of early exits at the Paris Masters, Alcaraz won the tournament for the first time in his career and is now just the Canadian Open title and the Shanghai Masters title away from completing the Career Golden Masters, a feat only Sinner and Novak Djokovic have completed in ATP history. Alcaraz’s nine-match winning streak has meant he enters the ATP Finals having played more tennis than any of his competitors, particularly Alexander Zverev, who crashed out in the opening round of the Paris Masters. As well as Alcaraz and Zverev, the ATP Finals lineup features Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli, Arthur Fils, Rafael Jodar, Frances Tiafoe and Ben Shelton. Cobolli, Fils, Tiafoe and Jodar are all making their ATP Finals debuts.

item.description: Balancing recovery and match fitness A pair of ripped shorts, nine goals and plenty of minutes for the youngsters: T hursday’s friendly against Mladá Boleslav certainly wasn't short on talking points. Speaking to the media afterwards, our sporting director Sebastian Schuppan reflected on the game and discussed individual player development, the challenges ahead and Assan Ouédraogo . Match fitness more important than the result After four consecutive weeks of midweek fixtures , with nine games in just 35 days, and with 11 first-team players away on international duty, the friendly against the Czech top-flight side was primarily about giving players valuable minutes. Eight players from our U19s were involved, while several first-team players also got a full 90 minutes under their belts, including Maxime Estève , Lukas Klostermann , Rocco Reitz and Johan Bakayoko . “The focus during this international break is on giving the lads who haven't played as much recently some good training sessions and a chance to get back into a rhythm ,” explained Schuppan. Despite the defeat, he felt the game had served its purpose. “It's more about the players' individual development and giving them minutes on the pitch,” he stressed. A wardrobe malfunction proves costly That said, the Red Bulls obviously weren't happy with the result, particularly as the decisive goal came late on while the hosts were temporarily down to ten men . Estève, who had earlier scored to make it 2-2, ripped his shorts in a challenge. The French defender had to leave the pitch to change, and Boleslav took advantage of his absence . Schuppan wasn't particularly amused by the incident. “ It was a bit unfortunate. I would've liked the referee to wait a moment in that situation. It's not something that happens very often.” Still, he acknowledged that in a friendly, it was “not the end of the world.” Recharging the batteries for the final stretch Our lads have certainly had plenty of competitive action in recent weeks . That was also why the likes of Castello Lukeba and captain David Raum weren't included in the squad for the friendly. “The lads have had a busy workload recently and have played the full 90 minutes almost every time,” explained Schuppan. “So this was an opportunity to give them a bit of a breather and let them follow individual training programmes.” The demanding schedule was also behind Neil El Aynaoui' s early return from international duty with Morocco due to a minor calf problem. “It's nothing serious. A year later, he was traded. Could Naz Reid be on the move again? While it’s no secret at this point that the transition for Naz to Hornets “culture” has been tough. However, according to Jon Krawczynski (The Athletic) , things are already so bad that “the possibilities of Naz getting traded are very high.” “The Hornets now are clearly in a period of transition, and they decided that LaMelo [Ball] was not going to be a part of the team that they believe can eventually get to real contender status. They made a decision with that core group that they were not good enough as constructed, and so they had to take a step back, amass some assets and go forward and what that also means means is…the possibilities of Naz getting traded again are very high. item.title: Rory McIlroy opens DP World Tour Championship with 69 to boost bid for record-tying Race to Dubai title
item.description: DUBAI, United Arab Emirates — Rory McIlroy started the strongest of the Race to Dubai title contenders at the season-ending World Tour Championship on Thursday, shooting 3-under 69 to lie in third place and two strokes off first-round leader Joost Luiten. McIlroy is seeking to claim the year-long award — crowning the best No. 1 player on the European tour that season — for a record-tying eighth time, and for the fifth straight year. He is guaranteed to do so with a victory at Jumeirah Golf Estates this week. The world No. 2 is second in the Race to Dubai standings behind Eugenio Chacarra , who shot 72 and was already three strokes behind McIlroy. They were in the final pairing on Thursday and McIlroy underlined his first-round superiority on the par-5 No. 18 with a 254-yard approach to 13 feet that set up a tap-in birdie, while Chacarra laid up from the rough and had to settle for par. “Anything in the 60s today I felt was a good score,” McIlroy said, a nod to the tricky conditions at the Earth course because of crosswinds and punishing thick rough lining the fairways and around the greens. “And sort of held it together nicely when I needed to.” Chacarra, playing his first year on the tour, acknowledged he was at a disadvantage against McIlroy and others who “have played this course a million more times.” “I know I need to do a couple of things better to be able to have a chance on Sunday, and that’s what I’m going to focus on,” the Spaniard said. “If I fix those, a little strategy-wise, and I can putt a little better, I think I’m going to have a chance on Sunday.” Patrick Reed, third in the Race to Dubai standings and the other realistic title contender, failed to turn around his recent slump in form and shot 75. After dropping a shot at No. 14 for his fourth bogey of the day, the American appeared to toss his putter toward his bag in frustration as he headed to the next tee. Jon Rahm, the champion in Abu Dhabi last week who needs to win again and hope for Chacarra and McIlroy to finish way down the leaderboard, opened with 71. PGA Tour cards up for grabs Luiten handled the tough conditions the best. He went out in 31 after five birdies in his front nine and was even par coming home, with a 6-foot birdie putt at the par-5 18th wrapping up a round of 67. With so many points on offer this week, a win also would come with a huge reward for any outsider like Luiten. That’s because up for grabs this week are 10 places on next season’s PGA Tour available to European tour members who are not otherwise exempt. Luiten isn’t currently one of those 10. He was a stroke clear of Jakob Skov Olesen, who is among those in line for a PGA Tour card. Victor Perez, Gregorio De Leo, Freddy Schott and Francesco Laporta were alongside McIlroy a further shot back after their 69s.
